quests.hint: MAKING PEOPLE NOTICE OR LOOK AT SOMETHING SPECIFIC
quests.explanation: DRAW ATTENTION means to make people notice something. DRAW is also used with draw a conclusion and draw a crowd.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: STARTING A HEATED PUBLIC DISAGREEMENT ABOUT SOMETHING
quests.explanation: SPARK CONTROVERSY means to start a heated public disagreement. SPARK is used here as a verb, meaning to trigger or set off.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: CAUSING PEOPLE TO START ARGUING ABOUT DIFFERENT SIDES OF AN ISSUE
quests.explanation: IGNITE DEBATE means to cause people to start arguing about an issue. IGNITE literally means to set on fire, used here figuratively.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: CAUSING PEOPLE TO GUESS AND SPREAD THEORIES WITHOUT CONFIRMED FACTS
quests.explanation: FUEL SPECULATION means to cause people to guess and spread theories. FUEL is used here as a verb, meaning to feed or encourage.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: CAUSING OFFICIALS TO START LOOKING INTO A SITUATION FORMALLY
quests.explanation: PROMPT AN INVESTIGATION means to cause officials to formally look into something. PROMPT is used here as a verb, meaning to trigger.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: BEING SERIOUS ENOUGH THAT PEOPLE SHOULD REASONABLY WORRY ABOUT IT
quests.explanation: WARRANT CONCERN means to be serious enough to justify worry. WARRANT is used here as a verb, meaning to justify or deserve.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: EXPLAINING WHY MONEY SPENT WAS NECESSARY AND REASONABLE
quests.explanation: JUSTIFY AN EXPENSE means to explain why spending money was necessary. JUSTIFY is also used with justify a decision and justify an action.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: DOING BETTER THAN WHAT PEOPLE THOUGHT WAS POSSIBLE
quests.explanation: EXCEED EXPECTATION means to do better than people thought possible. EXCEED is also used with exceed a limit and exceed a budget.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: FAILING TO REACH A STANDARD OR GOAL THAT WAS EXPECTED
quests.explanation: FALL SHORT means to fail to reach an expected standard or goal. FALL is used in many two-word phrases, such as fall apart and fall behind.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: MEETING THE HIGH STANDARD OR EXPECTATIONS THAT PEOPLE HAVE FOR YOU
quests.explanation: LIVE UP TO expectations means to meet the standard others expect of you. LIVE is also used in live through and live off, both meaning to endure or survive using something.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: BEING AS GOOD AS THE STANDARD YOU ARE BEING COMPARED TO
quests.explanation: MEASURE UP means to be as good as a required standard. MEASURE is also used in measure out, meaning to carefully portion something.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: COMPARING WELL AGAINST OTHER OPTIONS OR COMPETITORS
quests.explanation: STACK UP FAVORABLY means to compare well against alternatives. This phrase often appears as stack up favorably against, as in comparing prices or products.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: CAREFULLY THINKING ABOUT THE DIFFERENT CHOICES BEFORE DECIDING
quests.explanation: WEIGH YOUR OPTIONS means to carefully consider different choices before deciding. WEIGH is also used with weigh the pros and cons.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: JOINING A CONVERSATION TO ADD YOUR OWN OPINION
quests.explanation: CHIME IN means to join a conversation with your own comment. CHIME is normally the sound a bell makes, used here to mean speaking up.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: GIVING UP YOUR POSITION IN AN ARGUMENT INSTEAD OF CONTINUING TO FIGHT FOR IT
quests.explanation: BACK DOWN means to give up your position rather than continue arguing. BACK is also used in back up, meaning to support someone or reverse a vehicle.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: REFUSING TO CHANGE YOUR POSITION, EVEN WHEN OTHERS DISAGREE WITH YOU
quests.explanation: STAND FIRM means to hold your position despite pressure to change. STAND is also used in stand up for, meaning to defend or support something.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: REFUSING TO RETREAT OR GIVE UP YOUR POSITION UNDER PRESSURE
quests.explanation: HOLD YOUR GROUND means to refuse to retreat under pressure. The opposite, lose ground, means to fall behind or weaken your position.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: FALLING BEHIND OR WEAKENING YOUR POSITION LITTLE BY LITTLE
quests.explanation: LOSE GROUND means to fall behind or weaken your position over time. This is the opposite of hold your ground.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: CLOSING THE DISTANCE BETWEEN TWO VERY DIFFERENT SIDES OR IDEAS
quests.explanation: BRIDGE THE GAP means to close the distance between two different sides or ideas. BRIDGE is used here as a verb, meaning to connect.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: REDUCING THE NUMBER OF CHOICES OR CANDIDATES YOU ARE CONSIDERING
quests.explanation: NARROW THE FIELD means to reduce the number of choices or competitors. NARROW is used here as a verb, meaning to make smaller.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: MAKING A COMPETITION FAIR SO EVERYONE HAS AN EQUAL CHANCE
quests.explanation: LEVEL THE PLAYING FIELD means to make a competition fair for everyone. The phrase comes from sports, where an uneven field would give one team an advantage.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: TIPPING THE BALANCE SO ONE SIDE CLEARLY WINS OR IS PREFERRED
quests.explanation: TIP THE SCALE means to shift the balance so one side wins or is favored. The phrase comes from an old-fashioned weighing scale.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: COMPLETELY REVERSING THE DIRECTION A SITUATION WAS HEADING IN
quests.explanation: TURN THE TIDE means to reverse the direction a situation was heading, especially from losing to winning. The phrase comes from the ocean's tides changing direction.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: DECIDING TO DO SOMETHING DIFFERENTLY THAN YOU WERE PLANNING TO
quests.explanation: CHANGE COURSE means to switch to a different plan or direction. CHANGE is also used with change your mind and change direction.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: TAKING A DIFFERENT PATH TO GET SOMEWHERE THAN THE ONE ORIGINALLY PLANNED
quests.explanation: ALTER YOUR ROUTE means to take a different path than originally planned. ALTER is also used with alter a plan and alter an appearance.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: PLANNING A CLEAR PATH FORWARD FOR THE FUTURE
quests.explanation: CHART A DIRECTION means to plan a clear path forward. CHART is used here as a verb, meaning to map out carefully.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: DELIBERATELY AVOIDING SOMETHING OR SOMEONE THAT COULD CAUSE PROBLEMS
quests.explanation: STEER CLEAR OF means to deliberately avoid something. STEER is normally used for guiding a vehicle, used here to mean guiding your own actions.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: SUDDENLY CHANGING DIRECTION AWAY FROM THE PATH YOU WERE ON
quests.explanation: VEER OFF means to suddenly change direction away from your path. VEER is often used for vehicles, as in the car veered off the road.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: SLOWLY BECOMING LESS CLOSE TO SOMEONE OVER TIME, WITHOUT ANY SINGLE BIG EVENT
quests.explanation: DRIFT APART means to slowly become less close to someone. DRIFT is also used with drift off, meaning to slowly fall asleep.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.

quests.hint: SLOWLY FEELING LESS EMOTIONALLY CLOSE TO SOMEONE YOU USED TO BE NEAR
quests.explanation: GROW DISTANT means to slowly feel less emotionally close to someone. This is similar to grow apart, though grow distant often describes just one side pulling away.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
